issues.description: Exercises 2.6, 4.6, and 5.6 require returning “simulation counts”, but the provided reference implementations run the circuits on Aer.get_backend("statevector_simulator") and then call result.get_counts(qc). This is inconsistent with the usual Qiskit workflow taught to learners: counts are produced by shot-based sampling backends (e.g., qasm_simulator/AerSimulator) after measurement, whereas a statevector simulator is primarily for retrieving statevectors. The mismatch can confuse students about which backend to use and why counts are available.
issues.suggestedFix: For Exercises 2.6/4.6/5.6, switch simulate() to a sampling backend (e.g., Aer.get_backend("qasm_simulator") or AerSimulator()) and keep shots-based execution to obtain counts. Alternatively, if you want to keep statevector_simulator, update the problem statement and function contract to return a statevector/probabilities instead of counts.

issues.description: In the Exercise 5 template, GroverKakuro.state_preparation(...) names its third parameter `ancilla_register`, while the class attributes, other methods (oracle/diffusion/grover_circuit), and the reference solution consistently call it `auxiliary_register`. This naming inconsistency can mislead students into thinking two different registers are involved and causes unnecessary mapping when following the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template parameter `ancilla_register` to `auxiliary_register` in GroverKakuro.state_preparation(...), and ensure the docstring uses the same term consistently.
